utterances.text: Did you see a picture or did you just see a paper with something on it or were you able to make out what was on the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not able to make out anything on the picture whatsoever, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You cannot say for certain that you saw the picture of a person throwing out a bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said at page 12, line 18 of your testimony today that this photograph was provided by the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the basis for your assertion that it was provided by the Bosnian side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told that by the Americans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it is not your own personal knowledge. You were told.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few more questions for you. The Americans that told you that it was provided by the Bosnian side, were that the same Americans that told you what was depicted on that photograph but which you couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to go back to P - what was it? - 868 and to page 54 and I need the B/C/S only. This, again, is a picture of the Markale market as it was in the past. Witness, do you see that there is behind the stalls that there is a lower construction -- it's perhaps difficult to see. Whether it's one or two floors up or even three. Is that where you gained the impression that it may have been thrown from those buildings or from, rather, from what we see further in the back or to the right or to the left, which are higher up buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it would have been the -- the building to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The building where we see above the stalls at least four floors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I then take you to page 27 of the same document. Witness, here are some measurements on what still is said to be the Markale market. The building you pointed at - but I'm speaking agreement of the parties - would be building number 5, if I ... Any disagreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it might be number 2, actually, based upon if the representations of the three equally spaced rectangles on the bottom are stalls, and if the three or four equally spaced rectangles along the middle of the page going from left to right are also stalls then I think building number 2 [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we go back to the previous photograph, page 20 -- page 54. And perhaps we could have them next to each other. That is, page 27 and 54. Witness, do you see the cursor on that? Could we move the cursor a little bit further to the right, further to the right. There. Is that where the cursor now, is that the building you referred to earlier when you said "the building to the right"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we then -- I'm again seeking the parties' input on whether that would -- in the understanding of the parties be anything else and that witness -- than building number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's our position that that is building 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that the Prosecution position. I am hardly well placed in the courtroom to now look at a document that was not announced to make any kind of representations. I just can't do that without having reviewed the record in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you presented a witness who tell us what happened on the Markale market from windows where possibly shells were thrown on the market but if you say you can't, at this moment, express yourself on it we'll have to do without. I'm drawing the attention of the parties to this one because there are more measurements, right or wrong, but there are measurements on this map which were not on the map that I showed the witness earlier. Witness, in view of the measurements, what is presented here as the point of impact is at metres and metres and metres away from that building you indicated. Do you have any reason to challenge the accuracy of what is depicted here compared to what you told us earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no -- one second, please. I'm just checking some of my sources. Yes, I'm not going to put any further questions, but for the parties to consider whether they would have any further questions, I draw your attention to P538, page 56, which gives more measurements, again right or wrong, but at least matters are measured there. I leave it to that for the time being. But if the parties would just check in order to see whether that would trigger any further questions, then they have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are any further questions, the parties may put them to the witness. If they need further time to look at the exhibit I just referred to, then they could ask for more time. Mr. File, any other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just have one question that follows directly from Mr. Ivetic's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at transcript page 31 of today's transcript, you said that you would have "sent a sitrep to Canada" regarding the photograph we were talking about. And then at transcript page 47 you said that this would have been a phone call to Canada. Without mentioning any names in open session, can you recall with any certainty the name of the person you spoke to on the phone when you called Canada?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't have anything further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. File. Then, Mr. Ivetic, before we allow the witness to leave the courtroom, first of all, we'd have to turn into closed session and then you want to address the matter you had on your mind in closed session as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In closed session or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we should initially be in closed session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now another matter, is there any chance - I don't know what you have on your mind - that we would need the witness for it any further or could you exclude that because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, the other matter has nothing to do with this witness. Right? Or, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm told we may need to have the witness here for the first part of the submission. The other part has nothing to do with the witness, so now I would ask that we go into private session and then I would defer to our friends from Canada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we would then first move into private session. Then we would -- once we've done with the witness we would move in closed session. And then we would deal with the second matter in closed session or should we return into open session then, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think once we have the discussion in private session we'll be able to then announce at a point that we go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness, I'll repeat what I just started saying. That is, that we'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. And I wish you a safe return home again. If you would wait until the curtains are down, then you may follow the usher and leave the courtroom and you are excused. We turn in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, should we proceed even with the curtains or should we wait for the curtains?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait for the curtains. People might not see you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. With relation to the videolink for this coming Monday both of the officers from the Canadian government that are with us today will be attending that videolink as per Your Honours' oral rendering of the permission to do so yesterday. We had originally scheduled that for 6.00 a.m. Canadian time which was 12.00 noon local time. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to deliver one decision. There is no need for you to remain present. We thank you for coming and for assisting in receiving the evidence we need. You are free to leave the courtroom, and the usher will show you out.

utterances.speaker: MS. WICKLER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would wish to stay, that's fine. It's all public. But as you wish. I would like to deliver a brief decision. I don't think that the screen is obstructing any view for anyone in the public gallery. I'll deliver the Chamber's decision on the admission of P7368, which is a newspaper article dated the 17th of November, 1995 and was marked for identification during the testimony of Drasko Vujic on the 4th of May of this year. The Defence submitted via an e-mail on 4 August that it objects to the admission of P7368 as Vujic opposed its content and was not familiar with the article. On the 31st of August, the Prosecution submitted - again via an e-mail - that P7368 should be admitted into evidence as Vujic recognised the author of the article and commented on the quality of his work. The Prosecution further submitted that Vujic also acknowledged that he had "encountered a small unit of Arkan's" in his area of responsibility as suggested in the article. The Chamber recalls the applicable law for the admission of evidence which is set out in Rule 89(C) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which allows a chamber to admit any relevant evidence which it deems to have probative value. The Chamber further recalls its guidance of 29 October 2012 transcript pages 4133 to -34, in which it explained that if the content of a document used during a witness's examination is sufficiently linked to the witness's testimony, the document can be admitted through that witness, even if the witness is unfamiliar with the document. P7368 discusses the area of responsibility of Arkan's Men, and Vujic testified that he had encountered a unit of Arkan's Men in that location. Therefore, the Chamber finds that P7368 is sufficiently linked to Vujic's testimony and that it is relevant and of probative value pursuant to Rule 89(C) of the Rules and, therefore, P7368 is admitted into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. As far as our programme is concerned, no witnesses available for -- further today and tomorrow, Mr. Ivetic.
